caption_method: Individual visual inspection of each saved reference; copy transcribed only when legible, uncertain detail described cautiously.

references.name: Alicent Hightower
references.medium: Designed type poster with distressed print texture
references.caption: A dark, symmetrical type specimen poster built from alternating black vertical bands and a deep oxblood-red field. The red areas are densely flecked with tiny irregular marks, like worn ink or a rough screenprint, and fade into near-black toward the centre. The huge two-line name, “Alicent Hightower,” is set in warm ivory high-contrast serif capitals and lowercase forms; fine ornamental swashes loop through and around the central letters, making the lettering itself the principal illustration. A small circular, engraved-looking monogram sits above the title, with the serif descriptor in one upper corner and the studio and OpenType labels in the lower corners. The title is clean and sharply edged against the granular background; the overall exposure is deliberately dark, with no photographic blur.

references.name: Mirales
references.medium: Fashion portrait photography with graphic type overlay
references.caption: A landscape editorial thumbnail built around a tightly cropped fashion photograph of a woman, framed from just below the face to the upper thighs. Her dark teal, finely textured dress fills the centre; one bare arm bends up along the left side and the other hangs along the right. Behind her is a warm taupe studio setting with a large pale, curved architectural or paper-like shape. Bright yellow “MIRALES” serif capitals run nearly edge to edge across the torso, with a small yellow studio line above and a descriptor and paragraph aligned across the lower area. Small publication labels sit in the top corners. The portrait is relatively sharp, with visible skin and fabric texture; subtle grain and low-key shadows give it an editorial film finish. The title is exceptionally high-contrast and remains the clearest element over the busy portrait.

references.name: Double Knuckle
references.medium: Close portrait photography with oversized serif typography
references.caption: A two-line ivory display title dominates a cinematic close portrait. “Double Knuckle” stretches across almost the full width, with a large curled opening swash on the D and extended, interlocking-looking terminals that push the words into one expressive lockup. Behind it, the photograph is split by the subject: a deep blue, softly mottled shadow field fills the left half, while a cropped person’s lower face, bare shoulder, and fine necklace occupy the upper-right and right edge. The skin is warm and softly lit; the face is cut off above the mouth, so the type remains the lead. A compact pale-gold serif credit sits beneath the title. The background has shallow-focus softness, fine grain, and muted exposure, while the pale title edges stay crisp and readable.

references.name: Mr. Fox
references.medium: Moody woodland photography with film-poster typography
copy: And His Peculiar Stroke of Luck
As Told by Himself Years After the Incident
references.caption: A cinematic literary-film poster set against a dim, misty woodland photograph. Dark leafy trees and a large trunk form a soft, uneven frame; an old metal pendant lamp hangs at the top centre and casts a small amber pool of light through the cool blue-green haze. The title “Mr. Fox” sits large in pale cream across the middle-left, its ornate M and long sweeping x flourish turning the name into the scene’s central graphic gesture. Supporting story credits are arranged in deliberate blocks at the upper-left, right, and bottom, with one nominee line at lower-left. A restrained warm accent is reserved for the lamp and selected copy. The forest is softened by haze and shallow focus; the title is sharp, exposed brightly, and separated from the darker foliage.

references.name: The Philatelist 1942
references.medium: Archival paper collage and distressed print
copy: He Was a War Hero and He Was a Heartbreaker
Not Based on a True Story
His Name Aroused Fear Among Men and Admiration Among Women
references.caption: A dense, red archival collage designed like an aged wartime or postal-history film poster. A rough crimson paper ground is covered in fine grain, faded black type fragments, clipped document edges, stamps, handwritten marks, and dark rectangular scraps layered at different angles. Across the centre, “The Philatelist” is set in enormous pale cream, high-contrast serif letters; “1942” anchors the lower-left of the title. Thin cream script moves diagonally above and below the main name, while a small production line and a two-line narrative hook sit near the top and bottom. Some background writing is intentionally obscured and fragmentary, like overprinted ephemera, while the title is crisp and fully exposed. The palette stays within oxblood, black, and aged ivory, with strong ink-on-paper contrast and conspicuous fibrous grain.

references.name: King’s Valley
references.medium: Landscape photography with large serif typography
references.caption: A warm monochrome landscape photograph of a broad mountain valley fills the frame. Layered ridges descend toward a faint river or path near the lower centre, with atmospheric haze softening the distant slopes. The whole image is tinted ochre, sand, and muted brown, giving the valley a late-afternoon or archival warmth. Huge ivory serif lettering spells “King’s Valley” across two stacked lines and nearly fills the canvas; the letters are sharply rendered and generously tracked in places, with distinctive curved terminals that remain visible against the terrain. Small typeface information sits at the top and bottom, and a cream pennant at the upper-right carries an alternates note. The photo is legible but slightly softened by haze and texture, not motion blur. Bright type against the darker land creates a clear, readable focal plane.

references.name: Return to Avalon
references.medium: Soft-focus atmospheric photography and poster typography
copy: In the Search for Excalibur Part II
references.caption: An intentionally pale, hazy film-poster composition with a faint photographic landscape or figure barely emerging behind the lettering. A cool grey-green field dominates, with soft clouded tonal shifts and a blurred dark vertical form along the far left. The oversized cream title “Return to Avalon” occupies most of the centre in two lines; the small scripted “to” is tucked between the words, giving the type hierarchy a deliberate pause. A pale pennant in the upper-right names the chapter, and narrow production lines sit above and below the title. The scene is high-key and softly exposed, with a washed, misty surface and fine grain. Unlike a sharply staged portrait, the background is intentionally defocused and atmospheric; the crisp ivory lettering carries nearly all of the immediate contrast and emphasis.

references.name: Peach Crush
references.medium: Botanical illustration and fruit specimen poster
references.caption: A fresh, confection-like fruit specimen built around a large illustrated peach. The round peach sits just behind the main title, shaded from warm yellow-orange at the highlight to saturated coral and red near its lower edge, with subtle stipple and print grain giving it a hand-rendered surface. Two dark green leafy branches arc in from the top and left edges, while another leaf-and-stem form anchors the lower-left. The oversized cream “Peach Crush” lettering crosses the fruit horizontally, staying clear through strong value contrast; a short product phrase is tucked at the right and a tiny designer credit sits over the fruit near the centre. The background is a flat pale blush pink. The illustration combines botanical engraving-like linework with soft colour transitions, so it feels tactile without photographic depth of field. The image is bright, cleanly exposed, and playful.

references.name: Replay
references.medium: Black-and-white action photography with retro type
copy: Inspired by the More Than Hundred Years Old Classic Cooper Black, Replay Has Soft and Rounded Old-Style Serif Typefaces from the Sixties Era
references.caption: A black-and-white action photograph of three people running across an open field forms a cinematic backdrop. The central runner is the clearest figure; near-identical figures at the left and right are softened with directional motion blur, suggesting repeated movement or a replay. A very large bright lemon-yellow “Replay” word in rounded, chunky display serif lettering dominates the middle and overlaps the runners. A narrow line of yellow text sits above inside three linked pill-shaped outlines, while a long italic yellow description runs along the bottom. The monochrome photo is darkened and grainy, leaving the yellow type as the strongest, most saturated element. The people remain recognizable but slightly blurred and subordinate; the oversized title is sharp and flat over the photo.

references.name: Eighties Comeback
references.medium: Fashion beauty photography and editorial serif typography
references.caption: A warm fashion-editorial photograph is cropped tightly around a woman’s lower face, lips, neck, and long blonde hair, which frames both sides of the image. The chin and lips sit at the top centre while the hair and skin create a soft, tactile backdrop across the full frame. Two enormous lines of cream high-contrast serif text—“Eighties Comeback.”—fill the centre and lower middle, with a smaller italic serif description directly beneath. A small outlined creator cartouche sits over the face above the title, and a bright mustard circular “New” badge sits at the upper-right. The photographic lighting is warm and even, with visible skin and hair detail and gentle grain; the face is cropped and partly covered by type by design. Cream lettering contrasts strongly with the darker hair and shadowed skin.

references.name: Rustique Serif
references.medium: Botanical and weathered-surface photography with specimen typography
references.caption: Large white serif letters spell “Rustique Serif” across two lines, filling most of a warm, shadowy photographic composition. The background layers a close-up of tall dried grasses or seed heads near the centre-left with dark foliage and worn vertical timber or metal slats at the right. Narrow vertical highlights and rusty brown bands add a weathered, tactile feel. A fine horizontal rule passes through the gap between the two title lines and continues to the right edge. Small white feature labels sit across the top, with the foundry and copyright details in the lower-right. The title is clean and bright; the image behind it is moderately dark, softly focused, and textured with subtle film grain. Light catches the grass and slats in a few narrow streaks, but most of the scene remains underexposed to protect readability.

references.name: Magic Whisper
references.medium: Dark fashion/character photography with ornamental display serif
references.caption: A near-black cinematic photograph presents a mostly shadowed human figure in ornate dark clothing, with small metallic or beaded details catching light near the head and torso. Tiny ember-like orange flecks drift through the surrounding darkness. The very large white title “Magic Whisper” is split across two tightly stacked lines and nearly spans the full width; elongated swashes and a looping central stroke connect the letterforms and make the name feel magical without adding separate ornament. A small white studio line sits above, while the descriptor below is bracketed by thin horizontal rules and four-point star marks. The figure and background remain deliberately low-exposure, almost silhouette, with selective highlights and slight grain. The white title is crisp, evenly lit, and sharply separated from the dark scene.

references.name: The Salieta
references.medium: Close-cropped fashion photography with vintage serif lettering
references.caption: A close fashion photograph fills the frame with the torso of someone wearing a thick charcoal knit sweater; the wearer’s face is outside the crop. A strip of brown hair falls down the left edge, while the ribbed, visibly looped sweater texture occupies the centre and right. The name “The Salieta” appears in oversized pale ivory decorative serif letters, with a smaller italic “The” perched over the much larger “Salieta.” An elongated flourish curls from the initial S and the final letter, and the name is set over the dark sweater so the cloth texture acts as a natural contrast field. A compact uppercase font descriptor and a handwritten studio credit sit below. The photo is softly lit, warm at the edges, and modestly grainy; the central type remains bright and sharp.

references.name: Design Maison
references.medium: Abstracted warm-toned photography with hybrid sans/serif typography
copy: Introducing a Brand New Display Typeface
A Hybrid Sans & Serif Display Typeface
references.caption: An oversized, two-line title, “Design Maison,” is set in a pale buttery yellow against a blurred, warm red-brown photographic field. The first word mixes a clean, light sans-serif “Des” with a flowing italic or script-like ending; the second word returns to a clean, rounded sans. This visible hybrid is the main typographic event. The background is abstract and out of focus, with a soft dark burgundy cloud near the upper centre, a rich orange-red middle, and a pale cream blur entering from the right edge. Fine grain and mild vignette soften the image. Small monospaced foundry and category labels align to the upper corners, a centered introduction sits above the title, and the typeface description and credits sit below. Warm cream lettering stays distinct from the darker red areas.

references.name: Quine
references.medium: Low-key glassware product photography with refined serif type
references.caption: A restrained, near-black product photograph shows several low coupe or cocktail glasses filled with a dark liquid. One glass sits partly behind the title at lower-left, another is prominent at lower centre, and a third is cropped by the lower-right edge; thin highlights reveal the curved rims and transparent stems against the darkness. An immense warm-white serif “Quine” stretches across the upper half, with its long Q tail sweeping below the word. “Modern Serif” sits close to the title at mid-right, while tiny category labels anchor the bottom corners. The scene is intentionally underexposed: most glass and background detail recedes into black, leaving only reflective edges and the pale type. The glass surfaces remain focused enough to read as real objects, with no heavy blur or added effects.

references.name: Neue Monique
references.medium: Minimal black poster with orange display type and wireframe illustration
references.caption: A stark black graphic poster uses a single hot vermilion-orange ink for the huge condensed title “Neue Monique.” The word is arranged across two tight lines and cropped close to the frame edges; its blocky vertical strokes occupy nearly the entire canvas. A fine white wireframe torus floats behind the upper-right of the lettering, its grid warped into a deep oval and partially hidden by the orange forms. Small white labels sit at the upper-right and along the bottom edge, while the foundry and collection details use orange at the lower-left and mid-bottom. There is no photographic background or material mockup: the contrast comes from flat black, orange, and white linework. Letter edges are sharp, and the single wireframe drawing supplies depth without cluttering the title.

references.name: Chunk Grotesk
references.medium: Pastel sky illustration with oversized black display typography
references.caption: A soft, dreamy sky illustration shifts from pale blue at the top through lilac and pink to warm cream near the bottom. Puffy, cloud-like forms enter from the upper-left and rise from both lower corners, with soft edges, subtle shading, and a lightly airbrushed texture. The enormous black name “Chunk Grotesk” is split across two lines at the top, set in ultra-heavy rounded grotesk letters with playful cut-ins and tight spacing; the text fills almost the full width and is cropped close to the upper edge. A small dark sans-serif studio label sits alone near the bottom centre, leaving a broad quiet stretch between title and label. The title is completely opaque and crisp against the pale sky. The background is high-key and gently diffuse, with no photographic blur or hard shadows.

references.name: Spektora
references.medium: Flat retro poster illustration and distressed ink
references.caption: A flat coral-orange poster pairs a very tall, tightly condensed black title, “Spektora,” with a screenprint-style penguin illustration on the right. The penguin is rendered in black and warm cream with rough halftone dots, speckling, and imperfect ink edges; its simple upright pose provides a character counterweight to the oversized vertical type. Three stacked black rectangular bars sit below the headline at left, each containing a large, narrow cream feature label. A small black studio/date block anchors the lower-right. The surface has restrained paper grain and minor print wear, while the palette stays limited to orange, black, and cream. The title and labels are flat, sharply outlined shapes; the penguin is the only detailed illustration. Contrast is very strong and the layout remains clean despite the text density.

references.name: Castrell
references.medium: Halftone portrait collage and warm retro type poster
references.source_note: The provided Creative Market transformation URL returned HTTP 403; this artwork was recovered from the matching Castrell product listing at Pixel Surplus.
references.caption: A mustard-gold retro font poster combines a cropped black-and-yellow halftone photograph on the left with a large, open yellow field on the right. The visible figure is cut off at the shoulders and legs, so it reads as a graphic silhouette and texture rather than a full portrait; dense black dot screens and rough ink distress create an aged print surface. The name “Castrell” crosses the middle in oversized pale-cream display letters with a heavy dark outline and offset shadow. Beneath and to the right, compact black lettering identifies the 1970s style and font. A large glyph-count number, small globe/certification mark, creator credit, and feature list are arranged in the upper- and lower-right. The warm yellow ground is grainy and imperfect; the title remains the strongest shape through scale, pale fill, and black edge contrast.

references.name: Grand Motley
references.medium: Color-blocked pop poster with outlined and layered typography
references.caption: A loud, flat pop-art poster is built from broad vertical rays of cream, yellow, royal blue, hot pink, and violet, all framed by a thick rounded yellow border. A bright green lower panel curves upward behind the title. “GRAND” appears in huge cream block capitals with a thick black outline and hard offset shadow; a sweeping pink script “Motley” overlaps it and repeats the dark shadow, turning the two font styles into one layered lockup. Yellow four-point sparkles punctuate the sides. Small type labels sit in opposite lower corners, and a yellow rounded plaque with black copy anchors the bottom centre. The shapes are clean and saturated, with almost no photographic texture; the dimensional effect comes from deliberate stacked outlines and offset ink, not realistic lighting. The crowded palette is controlled by bold black edges.

references.name: Palmora
references.medium: Upward-looking palm photography and white type
references.caption: A low-angle photograph looks straight up through several palm trees against a broad, vivid blue sky. One trunk enters horizontally from the left, while a taller trunk and wind-swept fronds cut diagonally from the top centre toward the lower-right; another cluster fills the top-right corner. Wispy pale clouds soften the open left side. Large clean white sans-serif letters spell “Palmora” across the centre, with a smaller descriptor tucked directly below and a compact white foundry mark near the bottom. The photograph is moderately grainy and slightly faded, with visible sky texture and palm detail; exposure is even, not dramatically dark. The title overlays both blue sky and dark leaves, using its solid white fill to remain readable across the changing background.

references.name: Pink Beach
references.medium: Retro screenprint illustration with textured color fields
references.caption: A retro beach poster is drawn entirely from a narrow palette of warm pink and deep blue-green. The pale coral-pink background has fine fibrous grain and a few slightly uneven printed edges. A dark teal palm tree leans inward from the upper-right, while layered, scalloped arch shapes frame the headline like a sunburst or vintage beach sign. Two wavy teal bands roll across the bottom as stylized water, with thin pink contour lines tracing their crests. “Pink Beach” sits huge in two lines, using thick, soft-edged, irregular display letters that feel hand-cut and gently warped. A small teal badge at the upper-left and a short descriptor below the title complete the composition. All shapes are crisp graphic forms with light print wear, not a photo; the dark type is strongly separated from its warm field.

references.name: Newake
references.medium: Geometric collage with gradient forms and grain
copy: The Original Font by Indieground Design
references.caption: A dense contemporary collage sits on a nearly black charcoal field with fine grain. The central cream title “Newake” spans the width in a bold, rounded geometric sans, crossing multiple graphic objects: a large blue rectangle, a glowing blue-to-magenta sphere above, pink and cobalt folded triangles, and a tall blue textured panel at right with parallel pink stripes. Small grids of white crosses, curved magenta chevrons, a fine looping line, and a small outlined globe distribute visual weight across the remaining spaces. Gradient lighting inside the sphere and blocks gives them soft luminous depth, while the title itself stays matte and sharply edged. Small foundry, certification, copyright, and glyph-count notes sit in a narrow bottom strip and at the corners. Strong cream-on-charcoal contrast holds the busy composition together.

references.name: Overprint
references.medium: Grunge type poster with hand-drawn illustration
references.caption: A near-black aubergine field is lightly worn with paper specks and faded, uneven ink. The giant warm-white title “OVER-PRINT” fills the upper and middle left in soft, chunky sans-serif capitals; letter edges appear rough and slightly distressed rather than perfectly geometric. A hand-drawn white mascot or character occupies the right side, with loose outlines and a gestural face; a large sketch-like leaf rises from the lower centre and overlaps the title’s lower edge. Small white sans-serif copy at lower-left describes the font feature, while a handwritten signature-style mark sits beneath the right illustration. The composition is intentionally asymmetrical, with the broad title balanced by expressive line art. Exposure is uniformly dark and flat; there is no lens blur, and the rough print texture gives the image its tactile depth.

references.name: Gentle Side
references.medium: Warm close-up water photography with soft display type
references.caption: A warm, close-cropped photograph shows a person’s skin partly immersed in rippling water. The body fills the right and central field, while dark water and wavering reflections gather around the left and lower edges. Coppery highlights skim the water surface and skin, giving the image a soft, intimate glow. “Gentle Side” is set in large, pale cream rounded sans-serif letters and broken across two centred lines; the title floats over the body and remains bright against the warm, mottled photograph. A very small, widely tracked descriptor and creator credit sit near the bottom. The photo is deliberately soft, with shallow focus and visible water distortion, while the type is clean and sharply rendered. Warm exposure, gentle grain, and the close crop make the image feel tactile rather than clinical.

references.name: Tokyo Marker
references.medium: Brush-lettering poster with ink texture and simple graphic badge
references.caption: A white paper-like field with faint wrinkles and soft grey folds supports a huge black brush-lettered “TOKYO.” Each letter is built from broad marker strokes with visible streaks, uneven ink density, dry edges, and occasional translucent overlaps; a long black underline reinforces the handmade gesture. Small condensed black labels sit at the far left and right. A large transparent vermilion-red circle intrudes from the upper-right, carrying stacked cream display copy and a faint brush or face illustration inside. The composition is high-key and sharply exposed, with the black mark as the dominant contrast and the red circle as the only saturated accent. The background remains mostly quiet so the rough ink texture is legible. No photographic scene or blur is used; the material character comes from simulated marker and paper.

references.name: FT Buck
references.medium: Flat cartoon landscape with shadowed display lettering
references.caption: A simplified Western-cartoon landscape places a deep green ground strip beneath a pale peach-to-pink sky that shifts into muted green at the horizon. A small cactus and low hills sit at lower-left; at right, a tiny pink-roofed house and a thin pole carrying a three-colour pennant punctuate the open field. The main name, “FT Buck,” is set in huge italic hot-pink display letters with a hard black outline and a heavy offset black shadow that makes it feel like a cutout sign. A small circled R floats above the first line. The lettering occupies the central field while the tiny landscape props stay peripheral. The scene is drawn in clean flat shapes with no realistic shading or photographic blur; the contrast between vivid pink, black, and green carries the image.

references.name: Portia
references.medium: Monochrome noir photograph with distressed title lettering
references.caption: A grainy black-and-white noir scene shows a lone silhouette standing at the edge of a narrow platform or rooftop on the far left. Thick smoke or fog curls upward behind the figure and fades into a dark, almost featureless background. The name “Portia” is set enormous in tall, high-contrast white display capitals, angled slightly upward and punctuated with oversized quotation marks. Narrow shadows and subtle wear make the letters feel printed into a vintage film poster. A small introductory line and noir descriptor sit above; production credit and a row of style names are arranged below. The image is intentionally underexposed, with the person nearly black and the fog carrying the only mid-grey detail. Heavy grain and soft smoky edges contrast with the crisp title.

references.name: Comicon
references.medium: Vintage comic-book speech-bubble illustration and halftone print
references.caption: A cream-coloured comic speech bubble with an irregular black outline fills most of the frame, set over a pale, visibly fibrous paper field. “COMICON” is placed in huge yellow comic lettering with a thick black outline and hard offset shadow; a second black handwritten phrase sits directly below inside the bubble. At the lower-right edge, a bright yellow starburst badge carries the six-typeface feature callout. A dense band of black halftone dots rises from the bottom, while a small shield-shaped Studio Works emblem sits above the bubble and widely tracked capitals span the top. The palette is limited to cream, black, and vivid yellow. Grain, dot screens, ink edges, and the oversized bubble make the piece read as printed comic packaging; the lettering stays sharp and high contrast.

references.name: Grotesk
references.medium: Minimal typographic poster with oversized abstract letterforms
references.caption: A wide, minimal poster uses a hard three-colour palette: pale electric aqua, near-black, and vivid red-orange. Giant black fragments of an extremely bold grotesk letterform are cropped so tightly that they become abstract vertical and circular shapes across the background. The red-orange word “Grotesk” runs horizontally over them in a much thinner, clean sans-serif, creating a deliberate scale and weight contrast. A narrow condensed white line below names the family range, and a small orange foundry credit sits beneath it. The composition has no image, object, texture, or lighting effects; its drama comes from scale, crop, overlap, and color. Edges are perfectly sharp and flat, with the oversized black forms acting as both background and type specimen.

references.name: Fonseca Grande
references.medium: Aged postcard collage with dimensional retro type
references.caption: An aged postcard design rests on a pale seafoam and cream paper ground with visible fibre, faded mottling, and fine speckle. The central title “FONSECA GRANDE” uses large warm-khaki block letters with a cream inline, dark outline, and thick offset brown extrusion; each word tilts slightly, like layered vintage sign lettering. A loose dark script “Greetings from” arcs over the first word. Around the title are small postal details: a red perforated stamp at upper-right, circular cancellation marks, a narrow red serial strip on the right, and tiny creator and type-effect notes. A muted turquoise phrase and olive maker’s badge sit along the lower area. The lettering is sharply legible, while the paper texture and printed marks feel faded and imperfect. There is no photographic subject; all depth comes from stacked ink and shadow.

references.name: Rose Tinted
references.medium: Pixel-art specimen poster with bitmap rose
references.caption: A limited-palette pixel-art specimen sits on a very dark burgundy field. The name “Rose Tinted” is rendered in huge white bitmap letters split over two lines; every corner and curve resolves into visible square pixels. A magenta-and-rose pixel illustration overlaps the upper-right of the title, with bright pink highlights on the flower and deeper purple shadow blocks in its petals and leaves. A narrow outlined progress bar below the name contains several filled rose-pink segments, followed by a small row naming the regular, italic, bold, and bold italic styles. Compact glyph-count and family notes anchor the lower corners. The image is flat and crisp, with no blur or lighting effects; its texture comes from the deliberate low-resolution grid and a restrained palette.

references.name: Spot Light
references.medium: Basketball action photography with athletic display typography
references.caption: An action photograph captures a basketball player dribbling on an outdoor court, cropped from the chest to the shoes so the face is outside the frame. The player’s bent arm, ball, shorts, socks, and shoes occupy the middle; a tall wire fence and dark green trees blur in the background. Two lines of vivid yellow italic display capitals, “SPOT LIGHT,” stretch across the player’s torso and ball, using a forward slant and tight fit to echo athletic motion. Small white feature labels sit in the upper corners, with short personality descriptors at both lower corners. The photo is moderately dark and desaturated, with the yellow type carrying the brightest exposure and strongest color. The background is softly focused, but the athlete, ball, and court remain recognizable.
